assumptions.summary: Highways are straight, lanes hold one vehicle across their width, and all vehicles have equal size.
Self-driving vehicles share real-time velocity and acceleration without communication delay while humans do not communicate.
Self-driving cars need no response time, although the later simulation uses a one-second response parameter.
Human and self-driving vehicles are each homogeneous classes.
A four-meter cell and one-second step adequately discretize position, speed and acceleration.
Eight percent of the daily count occurs during p peak hours and both regimes follow Poisson arrivals.
Response-time distance alone defines safe following distance.
Lane-changing safety follows the same class-dependent gap definition as following.
Cloverleaf transfers cross no traffic stream, so vehicles can disappear, wait and reappear.
Perfect autonomous control is the base case; a generic random acceleration/deceleration branch represents system error.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Daily segment count N, peak duration p and autonomous share q feed two arrival rates and class draws.
Figure 1 evaluates rates at N=200,000 while p varies.
Table 1 supplies human acceleration/deceleration probabilities by discrete speed.
Simulation uses a 250-cell, 1000-meter segment over a 24-hour generated traffic flow.
Initial factor runs fix 100,000 daily vehicles, equal directions, P_c=0.5 and p=1.
Traffic volume is varied from 100,000 to 500,000 at 30/50/70 percent autonomous share.
The real-data branch contains 224 segments from I-5, I-90, I-405 and SR-520.
The I-5/I-405 intersection sets all movement probabilities to 50 percent and T_inter=10 seconds.
The error branch perturbs acceleration or deceleration by one unit with stated ten-percent probabilities.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Two literature gaps select a hybrid representation rather than decorating a predetermined method.
Sensors and shared acceleration directly trigger the added state variable.
Dedicated lanes visibly harm low-share peak traffic before offering a small high-share gain.
The exact controller is recalled before coefficient sensitivity is interpreted.
A real fatal event reopens the perfect-system assumption and causes a new experiment.
The letter uses encourage-even-a-little and do-not-hurry because the two interventions have different evidence shapes.

language_observations.summary: Reusable human writing moves center on two-gap model selection, property-triggered state augmentation, actor cases before equations, signed-term explanation, diagram-before-inequality exposition, criteria-first experiments, adverse policy reversal, formula recall, real-failure stress, and unequal stakeholder imperatives.
the Summary exposes state extension, four model branches, real-data use and error testing: Make a layered simulator auditable before mechanics.
two literature gaps determine a hybrid representation: Retain the whole-road cellular structure and add variables needed for autonomous dynamics.
technology properties trigger state augmentation: Tie sensors and shared acceleration to adding acceleration as a cell attribute.
self-driving and cooperating are separated before combination: Distinguish accurate individual control from inter-vehicle data sharing.
cell semantics precede transition rules: Define spatial unit, occupancy type, speed, acceleration and valid states before updates.
one daily count becomes peak and nonpeak arrival regimes: Expose the split and its rate consequence before sampling.
an initial value is defended where selected: State why a low entry speed should wash out under uncongested acceleration.
three follower/leader information cases precede formulas: Make sensed and shared information explicit before control laws.
each feedback term is explained on both sides of zero: Translate formula signs into acceleration and deceleration behavior.
a lane diagram establishes actors before inequalities: Give gap symbols visual meaning before the eligibility and tie rule.
an interchange becomes disappear-delay-reappear: Explain a strong simplification as an event transformation.
capacity criteria are defined before factor plots: Bind passing time and density trace to the simulated segment and horizon.
one varied factor is surrounded by fixed settings: Make simulation curves comparable.
one plot pair supports several distinct judgments: Read slope, peak/day convergence, density mechanism and plateau separately.
a policy is implemented by two local model changes: Explain dedicated lanes through generation placement and lane-change restriction.
an adverse low-share result reverses the recommendation: Let reserved capacity harm low adoption before high-share benefit appears.
the real-data unit and aggregation are stated before charts: Trace 224 segments to road-average velocity.
a prior calculation is reused with a changed operating window: Avoid restating the pipeline while isolating peak hours.
the exact feedback rule is recalled before sensitivity: Reconnect coefficients to mathematical roles before reading curves.
a real failure reopens a perfect-system assumption: Turn technology maturity concern into a simulation branch.
the stakeholder letter uses different verbs for different evidence shapes: Say adopt early but do not hurry on dedicated infrastructure.
stakeholder prose retains the traffic mechanism: Connect sensors, shorter gaps, acceleration flexibility and communication to capacity.
an early imperfection question is closed in late sensitivity: Maintain one doubt across the model body.
the conclusion keeps three decision consequences: Compress adoption, dedicated-lane and factor-stability findings.

results_trace.summary: Passing time and vehicles present fall sharply at low-to-middle autonomous shares, then flatten by a metric-dependent share.
Three-, four- and five-lane curves converge as autonomous share rises.
At 30 percent autonomous share, three dedicated peak-hour lanes produce about 80 seconds and are worse than other cases.
At 70 percent autonomous share, dedicated-lane cases slightly outperform no dedication.
Traffic-volume penalty shrinks as autonomous share rises across the tested 100,000-500,000 daily range.
Whole-day road speeds rise fastest from low shares and flatten near high shares.
Peak speed gains are larger; peak density roughly halves from 10 to 50 percent before little further change.
P_c and feedback changes yield small directional effects, while random automation error increases passing time.

source.title: The Effects of Self-Driving Cooperating Vehicles on Traffic Capacity of Highways

source_quality.summary: All 25 physical pages were read and visually reviewed. The paper uses two literature gaps to justify an accelerated cellular automaton, separates human/mixed/cooperative following, exposes low-share dedicated-lane harm, aggregates 224 road segments, recalls formulas before sensitivity, and reopens perfect automation with a random-error branch before an asymmetric official letter.

decisions: which state extension represents autonomous control, how actor classes update, how traffic enters and crosses roads, whether automation reduces lane/volume pressure, when dedicated lanes help or hurt, and how imperfect systems change the result
inputs: autonomous percentage, lanes and daily volume

title: The Effects of Self-Driving Cooperating Vehicles on Traffic Capacity of Highways
unresolved_questions: The model is called feasible because outputs look consistent with expected autonomous-vehicle properties; independent calibration is absent.
Four-meter cells, one-second steps, identical vehicles and class-homogeneous behavior need discretization sensitivity.
Peak and nonpeak arrivals remain independent Poisson processes without overdispersion, serial dependence or entry blocking checks.
The 20 m/s initial speed is asserted harmless without warm-up removal or initial-condition sensitivity.
Safe distance T_r v omits braking distance, leader deceleration, road condition and vehicle class.
Human acceleration/deceleration probabilities are hand-selected without driver-data calibration.
The assumptions say self-driving has no response delay, while simulation uses T_rs=1 second.
Alpha, beta and gamma combine different physical dimensions and are set to one without scaling or stability analysis.
Acceleration lacks explicit physical bounds, jerk limits and a collision-proof invariant; update order is incomplete.
Communication is perfect and instantaneous until a later generic error test; latency and packet loss are absent.
Lane changes omit simultaneous conflicts, reservations, mandatory exits, route incentives and destination response.
P_c=0.5 is uncalibrated, and limited one-factor sensitivity does not validate the lane model.
The interchange uses one cloverleaf, 50-percent movement probabilities and T_inter=10 seconds without data.
A single 24-hour simulation per setting has no seed, replicate count, warm-up, Monte Carlo error or confidence interval.
Average passing time and vehicles present are called capacity although throughput and demand served are not reported.
Cars per second per kilometer mixes temporal flow and spatial density semantics.
Daily counts are divided evenly by direction without a directional data check.
The 224 segments appear equally averaged within roads; length-, volume- and direction-weighted alternatives are absent.
Visual equilibrium locations vary across Summary, Introduction, whole-day velocity, peak velocity and density.
The Summary says velocity doubles from 10 to 50 percent without binding the claim to a specific road/window denominator.
The 70-percent dedicated-lane divider comes from a sparse 30/50/70 grid and one five-lane setup.
Dedicated lanes becoming necessary is stronger than the small simulated gain and ignores cost, compliance, equity and induced demand.
One-factor P_c and a few alpha/beta/gamma combinations do not prove robustness or expose interactions.
The plus/minus one, ten-percent error process is not calibrated to observed failure types or rates, and total probability is ambiguous.
The official letter says communication can eliminate collisions, exceeding simulation evidence.
Reference 6 concerns orbital debris removal and appears unrelated to traffic cellular automata.
No code, raw output, seed policy, exact scheduler, collision assertions or runtime environment is released.
No dedicated strengths/limitations section exists; audit limitations must not be attributed to author self-critique.
